Many machines here are built with **Charged Redstone**. You make it by pushing power into a **Block of Redstone**. Here is how to charge your first one.
Power runs from the source, along the wire, into the redstone.
Mine **Energum Ore** for **Energum Dust**. Nine dust make a **Block of Energum**. It gives off %s SP of power every tick, forever.
Craft two **Outlets**. Place one on the Block of Energum and the other on a **Block of Redstone**.
Hold **Coated Wire**, right click one outlet, then right click the other to link them. One coil covers %s blocks.
The redstone fills up with power. At %s SP it turns into **Charged Redstone**. Mine it with a pickaxe to keep it.
With one Block of Energum a charge takes about %s seconds. Add more power to the network and it speeds up, down to %s seconds.
The **Heat Generator** needs Charged Redstone to build, so your first charge has to come from Energum.
Charged Redstone goes into many machines. Here are a few:
Hover an icon for its name.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.in: Every anomaly begins with a **rift**, a glowing tear in the air. Rifts are harmless. Each one hangs in place for %s to %s minutes and then closes.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.wh: About every %s minutes a rift may open %s to %s blocks from you. In the Overworld they always open up on the surface, even while you are down a mine.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ca: A new rift will not open while %s are already open within %s blocks of you, so collect them to make room.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.st: Craft a **Rift Detector** and hold it in either hand.
A panel next to your hotbar shows an arrow to the nearest rift and how far away it is.
Follow the arrow. The detector clicks faster as you close in.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ra: It picks up Faint rifts from %s blocks away and Abyssal rifts from as far as %s.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.finding_rifts.ti: The colour of the arrow and the detector's screen shows how **rare** the rift is, from Faint up to Abyssal. It is not the distance. The number on the panel tells you that.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.collecting_rifts: A **Rift Extractor** collapses a rift into an **Unstable Fragment**. It needs no power.
Get within %s blocks of the rift with a clear view. Even glass blocks the beam.
Hold right click and keep the beam on the rift. Faint rifts take %s seconds and Abyssal rifts take %s.
When the bar fills, the rift collapses into one fragment of the same rarity.
Faint, Wavering, Volatile, Severe and Abyssal. Rarer rifts are bigger and slower to pull in.
Look away and the beam drops. Get back on target quickly, because an abandoned rift slowly settles back.
An extractor lasts for %s rifts. Repair it with **Energum Dust** in an anvil.
Fragments stack up to %s. Keep them, because the **Archive Terminal** turns them into anomaly files and stasis pods are built from them.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.archive_terminal: The **Archive Terminal** reads a fragment and prints the file of an anomaly tied to it. It needs no power.
Craft an **Archive Terminal** and place it. It stands two blocks tall.
Load one fragment and at least %s **Paper**, then press Roll.
Up to %s sealed files appear, each showing only its object class. Pick one and it prints as a **Sealed Dossier**. The others are purged.
Right click the dossier to break the seal and read it.
The fragment's rarity sets the odds. Faint fragments mostly find harmless Safe files, while Abyssal fragments lean toward Keter. The Threat Index on the screen shows the odds before you roll.
Each file prints only once per world. A sealed dossier stays harmless until someone breaks the seal, so it is safe to store or trade.
Build **The Database** to keep shared records. Use an opened dossier on it to file it. Everyone can then read the file or print a **Database Copy**, and copies never start anything.
Changed your mind about a file? Shred the unopened dossier at The Database and its file can turn up again.
Anomalies do not wander into your world by chance. An anomaly does not exist at all until someone breaks the seal on its dossier.
Breaking the seal opens an investigation in your name. Nothing shows up yet.
The anomaly arrives on its own schedule. Some come within minutes, others wait for the right moment.
Most come to **wherever you are** when that moment comes, not to the place where you opened the file. Moving away does not leave it behind.
Some point you to a place instead. The field notes in the dossier say where to search, and it shows itself once you get there.
A notice appears in the top left of every player's screen, and the investigator gets the exact spot in chat.
Some files bring a **mysterious stranger** instead. He finds you, talks with you, and hands the anomaly over, often sealed in a case. Wait out in the open and let him come to you.
Right click an opened dossier any time to check its field notes. On a server, if you log off, your open cases pass to a player who is still online.
Only break a seal when you are ready for what comes.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.containing_anoma: Once an anomaly turns up, keep it safe. Different tools suit different things.
A **Sealed Containment Case** holds one stack and keeps it inert. Sneak and right click with the item in your other hand to seal it in.
A **Storage Container** holds one catalogued anomaly. Open the door, then sneak and right click it to put the anomaly in. A **Tall Storage Container** fits bigger ones.
Containers can take a Heated or Cold Storage Upgrade and a glass front. Check each file to learn what its anomaly needs.
A **Stasis Pod** holds a living creature. Right click a mob to capture it and right click a block to let it out.
Pods are built around an Unstable Fragment. A Faint pod lasts %s minutes and an Abyssal pod lasts %s. Time only runs while something is inside, and when it runs out the creature breaks free.
Players, bosses and some anomalies resist stasis.
A **Containment Sign** labels a cell. Use an opened dossier on it to post that file. You keep the dossier.
Build cells from **Reinforced Containment Wall** and **Reinforced Glass**. Both shrug off explosions.
Some anomalies spread through the air. A **Gas Mask** or **Hazmat Hood** stops you catching them, but the agent settles on your suit instead.
When it happens you see "Your suit is contaminated". The suit then sheds a faint dust and spreads the agent to anyone within %s blocks.
Never take your mask off while contaminated. Everything on your suit bursts out around you, and you breathe it in.
Set a **Drain** into a ceiling and feed it water by pipe or bucket.
Stand in the stream below for about %s seconds, until you see "Decontaminated".
Only a drain pouring water works. Rain and swimming do not. Washing cleans the suit but does not cure an infection.
The mask or hood does the real work against airborne agents and toxic gas. A full hazmat suit also guards against a few anomalies.
Use a **Sterile Swab** on someone, or sneak and use it to swab yourself.
Feed the used swab to a **Bacterial Analyzer**. It is the only way to tell whether someone carries anything.
A used swab that picked something up is a live sample. Keep your mask on while you carry it.
Big machines leave dangerous leftovers behind. Handle them with care.
Toxic gas comes from reactor fuel towers, from vaporized waste water and from open vent ducts. In the open it forms green clouds that poison anyone without a mask.
Pipe your vent ducts into a **Gas Dissolver** and keep it topped up with water. It destroys the gas and scrubs clouds within %s blocks. It needs no power.
Never leave a vent duct open at the end. Gas pours out of open ends.
Reactors and the **Ore Purifier** make waste water. Swimming in it poisons you, and a drain pouring it scalds whoever stands below.
A **Vibration Chamber** cleans waste water back into plain water. It cleans %s mB per second using %s SP per tick.
A **Fluid Dump** gets rid of liquids fast, but dumping waste water or oil pollutes the water around it.
Polluted water turns murky and hurts swimmers once it gets bad, and a small pond can turn into waste water. Stop dumping and it slowly clears.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.intr: A network normally ends where its wires end. A **Network Hub** lets two or more networks share everything, no matter how far apart they are.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.flow: Each hub joins its own network. Hubs on the same port join those networks together.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.step: Build a hub at each site. It is a tower 3 wide, 9 tall and 3 deep, so clear the space first.
Put an **Outlet** on one of the copper ports at the base and wire it into the site network. The hub needs steady power, so use **Advanced Wire** or better.
Right click the hub and dial the same port on every hub that should talk. The panel lists the networks it reaches.
That is it. A computer at one site now sees the chat channels, drives and banks of the other sites.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.shar: Computer chat and message channels, upload port drives, point banks for the Shop, the archive database, and every wire signal: redstone senders and receivers, port ranges, speakers and sound consoles. Power is **not** shared, each site still needs its own.
These devices reach across linked hubs.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.dist: Hubs work across dimensions too. If the far site is not loaded, its live devices are out of reach and signals to it are dropped, but archive database access keeps working. The panel shows each far hub as **LINKED**, **UNLOADED** or **NO POWER**.
guidebook.scp_unleashed.network_hub.tip: Ports work like radio channels. Anyone with a hub on your port joins your network, so pick an unusual number.
Late in the project rifts can be farmed. A Rift Collector pulls them in by itself, and an instability grid makes them on purpose.
Place a Rift Collector and power it through an outlet on its base. It watches %s blocks around it.
When a rift opens in sight, the turret turns, locks on and pulls it in. Fragments wait inside for you or a hopper.
Range Upgrades stretch its reach to %s blocks.
Set four Instability Pylons on the corners of a rectangle, %s to %s blocks per side.
Power every corner. When all four are powered, arcs link the crowns.
Pick a target in any pylon screen and switch the grid on. It draws %s to %s SP/t.
Rifts form only inside the field, far faster than a matrix. A rectangle holds %s at a time, a box %s.
Stack a second rectangle %s to %s blocks above to build a box of eight pylons.
A grid can be armed for an apocalyptic charge. It asks for %s SP/t, will not move below %s SP/t, and takes at least %s minutes.
What it opens is golden, and it is not meant for the Archive.
